doc: Hand-made tables: identity permutation and every jitter 0.5, so the feature points form the lattice of cell centers and many distances tie exactly. At the center of a cell F1 = 0 and F2 = 1 (six neighbors tie at distance 1); on a cell face F1 = F2 = 0.5 (two features tie), at a corner F1 = F2 = sqrt(3)/2 (eight tie). A tie must give F2 == F1 (the second equal distance still counts as the second nearest). Tables are the inputs plan0.perm and plan0.jitter (seed null). Default tolerance. The permutation input plan<i>.perm is the draw as recorded (256 entries for Perlin3, 1024 for Worley3); the kernel indexes it DOUBLED, concat(perm, perm) (512 or 2048 entries, so p[i + 256] = p[i]): a port that indexes the stored array directly runs off its end (see the .table cases).
